info.title: punktfunk management API
info.description: Control-plane API for managing a punktfunk streaming host: host capabilities, runtime status, paired clients, the pairing PIN flow, and session control. Authentication: HTTP bearer token, enforced on every route except `/api/v1/health` when the host is started with a management token (mandatory for non-loopback binds).

delete.description:
Removes the client's certificate from the pairing store. Caveat: the nvhttp TLS layer
does not yet reject unlisted certificates (`gamestream/tls.rs` accepts any well-formed
client cert — a planned hardening step), so until that lands this removes the client
from the listing without severing its ability to reconnect.

parameters.name: fingerprint
parameters.description: Hex SHA-256 fingerprint of the client certificate DER (64 chars, case-insensitive)

404.description: No paired client with that fingerprint

get.description:
Lists every backend the host knows how to drive, flags which are usable right now, and marks
the one an unspecified (`Auto`) client request resolves to. Clients pass an `id` to their
`--compositor` flag (or `PUNKTFUNK_COMPOSITOR_*` over the C ABI) to request it.

200.description: Compositor backends with availability + the auto-detected default

get.description:
Lists the host's hardware GPUs, the persisted auto/manual preference, the GPU the next session
will use (and why), and the GPU live sessions encode on right now.

put.description:
`auto` restores automatic selection (`PUNKTFUNK_RENDER_ADAPTER` pin, else max dedicated VRAM);
`manual` pins capture + encode to the given GPU. Persisted across restarts; applies to the
**next** session (a running session keeps its GPU). If the preferred GPU is absent at session
start the host falls back to automatic selection rather than failing.

200.description: Preference stored; the new selection state

400.description: Unknown mode, or `gpu_id` missing / not a listed GPU

200.description: Host identity, versions, codecs, and port map

get.description:
Every installed-store title (Steam, read from the host's local files — no Steam API key)
merged with the user's custom entries, sorted by title. Artwork fields are URLs the client
fetches directly (the public Steam CDN for Steam titles).

get.summary: Fetch one cover-art image for a library entry
get.description:
Resolves `kind` (`portrait` | `hero` | `logo` | `header`) for the given library id and streams
the image bytes. For a Steam title, the host's own local Steam cache is tried first (exact —
it's what the user's Steam client already shows for it), the public Steam CDN's flat URL
convention as a fallback (newer titles' CDN assets can live at a per-asset-hash path the host
can't predict, in which case this 404s and the client falls through to its next art candidate).
Only Steam ids are backed today; any other store 404s.

404.description: No art of that kind for that id

post.description:
Creates a user-curated title (e.g. a non-Steam game, an emulator, a ROM) with caller-supplied
artwork URLs. The host assigns a stable id, returned in the body.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The custom entry id (without the `custom:` prefix)

404.description: No custom entry with that id

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The custom entry id (without the `custom:` prefix)

404.description: No custom entry with that id

get.summary: Local status summary for the tray icon
get.description:
Non-sensitive status (counts and booleans only — no PIN values, no fingerprints, no device
names). Unauthenticated, but served to loopback peers only.

200.description: Non-sensitive local host status (loopback peers only)

get.description:
The host's recent log entries — an in-memory ring of the newest few thousand, captured at
DEBUG and above regardless of `RUST_LOG`. Follow live by polling with `after` set to the last
response's `next` cursor; a `dropped: true` means entries were evicted between polls (the ring
wrapped). Bearer-only: logs can reference client identities and host paths, so this is part of
the loopback-only admin surface, never the LAN-readable mTLS one.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return entries with seq greater than this (omitted/0 = oldest retained)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max entries per response (default and cap 1000)

200.description: Entries after the cursor, oldest first

delete.description: Removes a punktfunk/1 client from the native trust store by fingerprint.

parameters.name: fingerprint
parameters.description: Hex SHA-256 of the client certificate (case-insensitive)

404.description: No paired native client with that fingerprint

get.description:
The native (punktfunk/1) pairing window. Poll while armed to show the PIN + countdown.
`enabled: false` means this host runs GameStream only (no `--native`).

delete.description: Closes the pairing window immediately (no new ceremonies accepted).

post.description:
Opens a pairing window and mints a fresh PIN to display. The user enters it on their device
within `ttl_secs`; the device then appears in the native client list.

200.description: Pairing armed; the response carries the PIN to display

503.description: Native host not available in this process

get.description:
Unpaired devices that tried to connect while the host requires pairing. Approve one to pair
it without a PIN (delegated approval); entries expire after ~10 minutes.

200.description: Devices awaiting approval (empty when none, or when the native host is not enabled)

post.description:
Pairs the device's certificate fingerprint — it can connect immediately (no PIN). Optionally
relabel it via the body; send `{}` to keep the name it knocked with.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Pending-request id from the pending list

404.description: No pending request with that id (expired?)

500.description: Could not persist the trust store

post.description: Drops the request. Not a blocklist — the device's next attempt knocks again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Pending-request id from the pending list

404.description: No pending request with that id

get.description: Poll this to know when to prompt the user for the PIN Moonlight displays.

200.description: Whether a pairing handshake is waiting for a PIN

post.description:
Delivers the PIN the Moonlight client is displaying, completing the out-of-band half
of the pairing handshake.

204.description: PIN delivered to the waiting handshake

400.description: Malformed PIN or unparseable JSON body

409.description: No pairing handshake is waiting for a PIN

422.description: JSON body does not match the schema

delete.description:
Kicks the connected client: stops the video/audio stream threads and clears the launch
state. Idempotent — succeeds even when nothing is streaming.

post.description:
Asks the encoder for an IDR frame on the active video stream (what a client requests
after unrecoverable loss — exposed for debugging).

get.description:
The full sample time-series of the capture currently recording, for live graphing. `404` when
nothing is armed.

200.description: The in-progress capture (meta + samples so far)

post.description:
Arms a new performance-stats capture. Idempotent: if a capture is already running this returns
the current status unchanged. While armed, the streaming loops emit aggregated samples (~ every
1–2 s) into the in-progress capture, readable live via `GET /stats/capture/live`.

get.description:
Whether a capture is armed, its sample count, and start time. Poll this (e.g. every 2 s) to
drive the capture-control UI.

200.description: In-progress capture status (idle when not armed)

post.description:
Disarms the in-progress capture and writes it to disk atomically, returning its summary. If
nothing was recording, returns `204 No Content`.

500.description: Could not write the recording to disk

get.description: Every saved capture's summary (the `meta` head only — not the sample body), newest first.
The full capture (meta + samples) for `id`, for graphing or download.

delete.description: Removes the recording `id` from disk. `404` if there is no such recording.

200.description: Streaming/pairing state and the active session, if any

ApiActiveGpu.description: The GPU live sessions are encoding on right now.

id.description: Stable id matching an entry of `gpus` (empty for the CPU/software encoder).

sessions.description: Number of live encode sessions on it.

ApiError.description: Error envelope for every non-2xx response.

ApiGpu.description: One hardware GPU on the host (software/WARP adapters are never listed).

id.description:
Stable identifier (`vendorid-deviceid-occurrence`, hex PCI ids) — pass to `setGpuPreference`.
Stable across reboots and driver updates, unlike an adapter index or LUID.

vram_mb.description: Dedicated VRAM in MiB (0 where the platform doesn't expose it).

ApiSelectedGpu.description:
The GPU the **next** session's pipeline will be created on, and why. (A preference change
applies to the next session; a running session keeps the GPU it opened on.)

source.description:
Why this GPU was selected: `preference` (the manual choice), `env`
(`PUNKTFUNK_RENDER_ADAPTER`), `auto` (max dedicated VRAM / platform default), or
`preference_missing` (a manual choice is set but that GPU is absent — auto-selected
instead so the host keeps streaming).

ApprovePending.description: Approve-pending-device request body. Send `{}` to keep the device's own name.

name.description: Operator-chosen label for the device (defaults to the name it knocked with).

fingerprint.description:
Optional: bind the window to ONE device fingerprint (hex SHA-256, e.g. from a pending knock).
When set, only a pairing attempt from that fingerprint consumes the window — so an unpaired
LAN peer can neither pair nor burn a window armed for a specific device (security-review #9).
Omit for an unbound window (any device may use the PIN — trusted-LAN only).

ttl_secs.description: Window length in seconds (default 120; clamped to 15–600).

Artwork.description:
Cover art for a title. All fields are URLs (the Steam CDN for Steam titles, user-supplied for
custom). The client prefers `portrait` for a grid and falls back to `header` when a title has
no 600×900 capsule (common for older Steam apps).

portrait.description: Vertical capsule / poster (Steam `library_600x900.jpg`). Best for a grid.

AvailableCompositor.description: A compositor backend the host can drive a virtual output on, and whether it's usable now.

available.description:
Usable on this host right now: the live session's own compositor, or gamescope wherever
its binary is installed.

default.description: True for the backend an `Auto` (unspecified) request resolves to right now.

id.description:
Stable identifier (`"kwin"` | `"wlroots"` | `"mutter"` | `"gamescope"`) — pass this to a
client's `--compositor` flag.

Capture.description: A full capture: summary + the sample time-series. The wire + on-disk shape.

CaptureMeta.description:
Capture summary — the filename stem plus the negotiated mode/codec/client. Stored at the head
of each on-disk recording and listed standalone (without the sample body) by
[`StatsRecorder::list`].

client.description: Short label / fingerprint prefix, or `""` if unknown.

CustomEntry.description:
A user-added title, persisted in `~/.config/punktfunk/library.json`. Same shape the API
returns and the web console edits.

id.description: Host-assigned, stable for the life of the entry (the `{id}` in the CRUD path).

CustomInput.description: Request body to create or replace a custom entry (no `id` — the host owns it).

GameEntry.description: One title in the unified library, regardless of which store it came from.

oneOf.description: How the host would launch it, when known.

GpuState.description:
Full GPU-selection state for the console: inventory, the persisted preference, what the next
session will use, and what is in use right now.

oneOf.description: The GPU live sessions use right now (absent while nothing is streaming).

env_override.description:
`PUNKTFUNK_RENDER_ADAPTER` (the host.env pin), when set — it applies while `mode` is
`auto`; a manual preference overrides it.

preferred_available.description: Whether the preferred GPU is currently present.

preferred_id.description:
The manually preferred GPU's stable id, when one is stored (kept while `mode` is `auto` so
a console can offer returning to it). May reference a GPU that is currently absent.

preferred_name.description: The stored name of the preferred GPU (a usable label even when it is absent).

oneOf.description: The GPU the next session will use.

HostInfo.description: Host identity and advertised capabilities (static for the life of the process).

app_version.description: GameStream host version advertised to Moonlight clients.

gfe_version.description: GFE version advertised to Moonlight clients.

uniqueid.description: Stable per-host id (persisted across restarts), matched on pairing.

value.description: The appid (for `steam_appid`) or the shell command (for `command`).

LocalSummary.description:
Non-sensitive host status for the local tray icon: counts and booleans only — no PIN values,
no fingerprints, no device names. Served unauthenticated to LOOPBACK peers only (see
`require_auth`): the bearer-token file is SYSTEM/Administrators-DACL'd on Windows, so the
per-user tray process cannot authenticate — this narrow read-only route is its status source.

audio_streaming.description: True while the audio stream thread is running.

paired_clients.description: Number of pinned (paired) GameStream client certificates.

pending_approvals.description: Native pairing knocks awaiting the operator's approval (count only).

pin_pending.description: True while a GameStream pairing handshake is parked waiting for the user's PIN.

oneOf.description: The active launch session (set by Moonlight's `/launch`, cleared on cancel/stop).

video_streaming.description: True while the video stream thread is running.

msg.description: The formatted message, structured fields appended as `key=value`.

seq.description: Monotonic sequence number (1-based) — pass the last one back as the `after` cursor.

LogPage.description: One poll's worth of log entries.

dropped.description: True when entries between `after` and the first returned one were already evicted.

next.description: Cursor for the next poll (the last returned seq, or the request's `after` when empty).

fingerprint.description: Hex SHA-256 of the client certificate — its stable id here.

name.description: The name the client supplied when pairing.

NativePairStatus.description:
Native (punktfunk/1) pairing status. Unlike GameStream, the **host** mints the PIN (the SPAKE2
ceremony needs it client-side first), so the console **displays** `pin` for the user to enter on
their device — armed on demand for a short window.

armed.description: True while a pairing window is open.

enabled.description: Whether the native host is running (the unified host started with `--native`).

expires_in_secs.description: Seconds left in the window (null = disarmed, or armed with no expiry via the CLI flag).

pin.description: The PIN to display while armed (null when disarmed).

fingerprint.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the client certificate DER — the client's stable id here.

subject.description: Certificate subject (e.g. `CN=NVIDIA GameStream Client`), if the DER parses.

pin_pending.description: True while a pairing handshake is parked waiting for the user's PIN.

PendingDevice.description:
An unpaired device that tried to connect while the host requires pairing — awaiting
**delegated approval** (approve it here instead of fetching the host PIN out of band).

age_secs.description: Seconds since the device last knocked.

fingerprint.description: Hex SHA-256 of the device's certificate — what approval pins.

id.description: Id to address approve/deny (per-process; entries expire after ~10 minutes).

name.description: Best-effort device label (the client's own name, else fingerprint-derived).

PortMap.description:
Every port a client integration may need (Moonlight derives the stream ports from the
HTTP base; a control pane should not have to).

RuntimeStatus.description: Live host status (changes as clients launch/end sessions).

audio_streaming.description: True while the audio stream thread is running.

pin_pending.description:
True while a pairing handshake is parked waiting for the user's PIN
(submit it via `POST /api/v1/pair/pin`).

oneOf.description: The active launch session (set by Moonlight's `/launch`, cleared on cancel/stop).
The RTSP-negotiated stream parameters (present once a client has completed ANNOUNCE).

video_streaming.description: True while the video stream thread is running.

SessionInfo.description: Client-requested launch parameters (key material is never exposed here).

gpu_id.description:
Required when `mode` is `manual`: the stable `id` of a currently listed GPU
(see `listGpus`).

mode.description: `auto` (env pin, else max dedicated VRAM — the default) or `manual`.

StageTiming.description: One pipeline stage's latency in an aggregation window (microseconds).

StatsSample.description: One aggregated sample (~ every 2 s native, ~ every 1 s GameStream).

fps.description: Genuine NEW frames/s from the source.

packets_dropped.description: Packets dropped this window (receiver-side / reassembler, where known).

send_dropped.description: Host send-buffer overflow / EAGAIN this window (delta).

stages.description: Ordered pipeline stages for this path.

t_ms.description: Milliseconds since capture start (monotonic; stamped by [`StatsRecorder::push_sample`]).

StatsStatus.description: Snapshot of the in-progress capture for the management API.

kind.description: Path of the in-progress capture (`""` if idle).

started_unix_ms.description: Unix start time of the in-progress capture (`0` if idle).

min_fec.description: Client's parity floor per FEC block (`minRequiredFecPackets`).

SubmitPin.description: The PIN Moonlight displays during pairing.
